page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-4 is a flexible compute instance powered by the ARM64 Ampere AmpereOne-M processor architecture (Ampere-1a model). The configuration provisions 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at an operational clock speed of 2.0 GHz, eliminating hyperthreading interference through single-threaded physical core assignment. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB total, delivering an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration includes support for ARM AES instructions, while hardware extensions such as AVX or AMX are not part of the standard ARM instruction set. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, depending entirely on remote block storage attachments, and provides one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent baseline single-thread capability alongside low overall aggregate capacity due to the low core count. The Geekbench single-core evaluation achieved 1381.0, reflecting middle-tier performance, while the multi-core result of 2484.0 and stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 1696.29 place it in lower percentiles. Memory performance shows 211.33 GB/sec under small cached block conditions, dropping to 20.66 GB/sec on large uncached read workloads, with uncached writes maintaining 26.37 GB/sec. Data manipulation tasks demonstrate moderate efficiency, with gzip compression recording 28.59 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing achieving 1615.0. Redis key-value operations reach 3.82 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput registers at 4.61 GB/sec.

Given the absence of local storage and modest compute density, this instance offers balanced resource utilization for entry-level workloads rather than sustained compute-heavy tasks. The low memory ceiling limits large in-memory databases and dense microservices architectures. Workload suitability centers on lightweight edge tasks, low-traffic web serving, basic proxying, staging environments, single-threaded batch execution, and ARM-native continuous integration workers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-4 is an entry-level ARM-based flexible compute instance powered by a 2.0 GHz Ampere AmpereOne-M processor. Configured with 2 dedicated physical cores, 2 vCPUs, and 4.0 GB of system RAM, it provides a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio without hyperthreading overhead. The platform provides hardware AES cryptographic instructions but excludes local storage disks, requiring remote volume attachments. Synthetic benchmarks register steady single-core throughput, logging 1381.0 in Geekbench single-core and 28.59 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside a multi-core score of 2484.0 and static web serving throughput of 4.61 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 20.66 GB/sec. Lacking GPU acceleration or integrated NVMe storage, this instance is suited for lightweight web serving, ARM software builds, microservices, and general staging infrastructure.
